newsitem.title: UK: Malaysia sees steady increase in cocoa production.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia sees steady increase in cocoa production.

text.p: Malaysia, one of the leading cocoa producers, expects a steady increase output until 1999 as it implements a rehabilitation programme, a government official said on Thursday.

The official, who declined to be identified, said Malaysia's cocoa crop in 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) would be higher at 130,000 tonnes from an estimated 126,000 tonnes in the previous year as the results of the government programme.
"There is going to be a modest recovery in the production of cocoa in Malaysia," the official said on the sidelines of the International Cocoa Organisation (ICCO) meeting.

The ICCO and traders have estimated Malaysia's 1995/96 output lower at between 105,000 and 110,000 tonnes. "We...expect to see the production increase to 140,000 tonnes in 1997/98 while in 1998/99 we see cocoa crop production at 150,000 tonnes," said the official at the ICCO meeting.
The official said the rehabilitation programme was mainly aimed at smallholders who produced more than 50 percent of Malaysia's cocoa, adding that it had motivated higher production.
He said Malaysia also planned to expand its cocoa plantations, located mainly in the region of Sabah, to become 215,000 hectares. He gave no other details.
The Malaysian official said his country was confident of maintaining a steady growth in cocoa output because diseases such as pod borer were also under control.
"Pod borer is under control and it is not very serious," he added.

He said that the government was implementing biological control to ensure good production, adding that the main concern for Malaysia for the time being was to meet domestic need as the country still had to import cocoa.
He also said he expected consumption to increase in Malaysia in the coming years boosted by the people's higher income.
"We expect consumption to increase in the coming years as the economy is getting higher and people can expect better income," he said.

Cocoa traders in Asia have predicted that chocolate consumption in the region as a whole would grow by at least 20 percent a year in the coming years as economies boom. - London Newsroom, +44 171 5452 8072
